national_raw_news.content: The Election Commission today said that Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will visit the homes of individuals who have been issued notices during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to collect the required documents. The BLOs will subsequently upload the documents on the ECINet platform. The decision was taken during a meeting held by the Election Commission in New Delhi. The Commission clarified that such persons will not be called for hearing by the Electoral Registration Officer. It said that hearings will be conducted only in exceptional circumstances, preferably through online mode. The Commission also said that, if a hearing is required, the elector may authorize any adult member of their family to appear on their behalf. SIR has already been completed in 20 States and UTs, including Bihar and West Bengal. The Commission reiterated that the order for the SIR was issued for all the States and UTs with the unanimous approval of the Commission. The Commission said that any person whose name has been left out during SIR and wants to include their name can apply to the concerned Electoral Registration Officer. The Chief Electoral officer, District Election Officer and Electoral Registration Officer will immediately launch a special drive for enrolment of these electors. The District Election Officers will create adequate number of help desks and hold special camps for the people living in night shelters, labor, poor people and homeless. In view of the request received from CEO Delhi, the period for filing claims and objections has been extended by the Commission till 30th October. The period of disposal of notices and claims and objections has also been extended till 30th November this year.

national_raw_news.title: 24 mins ago | Sports 66 Kabaddi Golden Double: India wins men’s and women’s Kabaddi gold at Asian Games
national_raw_news.content: Both the Indian men’s and women’s Kabaddi teams today won gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 in Japan. The Indian men’s Kabaddi team clinched gold, beating Iran 40-34 at the Asian Games. The Indian women’s team also edged out Iran in a tense final clash, winning the contest by a 37-34 margin. India has made a strong medal haul at the Asian Games today, adding seven medals across Kabaddi, athletics, shooting and squash. Now India are currently placed 10th in the medal standings and its overall tally has reached 30 with four gold, twelve silver and fourteen bronze. In athletics, Tajinderpal Singh Toor won the silver medal in the men’s shot put with a throw of 20.64 meters. Sawan Barwal bagged silver in the men’s marathon ending India’s 44-year wait for a podium finish in the discipline, clocking 2 hours, 11 minutes and 37 seconds. His performance marked a personal best and a new national record. In shooting, Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa K. Vinod and Ashi Chouksey secured silver in the women’s 50-metre rifle three-position team event, scoring 1,763 points. Prachi Chaudhary win bronze in women’s 400m with a timing of 53.21 seconds. In mixed doubles squash, Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar bagged bronze. President Droupadi Murmu has extended her greetings to the Indian Men’s Kabaddi Team on winning the Gold Medal at the 2026 Asian Games. In a social media post, the President highlighted that with both the Men’s and Women’s teams securing top honours, India has achieved a historic golden double sweep in Kabaddi. The President praised the athletes, stating that this twin victory showcases the team members’ exceptional skill, composure, resilience, and outstanding teamwork that paved the way for India’s triumph.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi congratulates players for securing victory in the Asian Games 2026 46 mins ago 35
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated players for securing victory in the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, Mr Modi congratulated Prachi Choudhary on winning the Bronze medal in the Women’s 400 meter at the Asian Games. He said that her excellent performance has earned India a memorable place on the podium. The Prime Minister also congratulated Tajinderpal Singh Toor on winning the Silver medal in the Men’s Shot Put with an impressive throw. Mr Modi said that Tajinderpal has consistently brought laurels to the nation through his focus and perseverance. The Prime Minister added that Another Asian Games medal is a fitting addition to his remarkable journey. Mr Modi congratulated Manush Shah and Diya Chitale on winning the Bronze medal in the Mixed Doubles Table Tennis event at the Asian Games. He noted that this medal adds another proud moment to the rising popularity of Table Tennis in India. He said that their determination will inspire many young players to take up the sport and aim higher. The Prime Minister also extended greetings to Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa Vinod Kochalumkal and Ashi Chouksey. He congratulated them on winning the Silver medal in the Women’s 50 meter Rifle 3 Positions Team event at the Asian Games.

national_raw_news.title: Manipur observes 75th death anniversary of freedom fighter Lamyanba Hijam Irabot 1 hour ago 31
national_raw_news.content: Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh today said that the ideas and vision of freedom fighter Lamyanba Hijam Irabot, who worked tirelessly to unite the people of different communities residing in different parts of Manipur and bring them together as one, should continue to guide the people of the State today. In Manipur, the 75th Death Anniversary of Lamyanba Irabot was observed today across the State, remembering the pioneering visionary leader, communist politician and social activist of Manipur. Chief Minister Singh, while attending the main event at the Lamyanba Irabot Statue Complex in Imphal called upon the people to remember and honour the ideals and vision cherished by Lamyanba Irabot and ensure that these continue to inspire future generations. Shri Khemchand said that Lamyanba Irabot had raised his voice against the oppressive British rule and the prevailing social and political conditions from the 1930s onwards. He said that the valuable legacy left behind by the great leader should be carried forward by the present generation. During the event, the Chief Minister inaugurated several newly developed facilities at the complex and dedicated them to the people. He also led others in paying floral tribute to the statue of the great leader
